sadaf_hussain on October 6, 2026: "Photos from my trip to Jeddah in the last week of September. I was there for work, for fun, and to see the sights. It's not often that you get to visit a different world. You let go of a lot of thoughts, assumptions, stereotypes, and preconceived notions, and then they all fall apart, leaving you with a completely new experience. My trip was really great.

You'll see more photos in the coming days. Prepare yourself 😁.".

134 likes, 0 comments - sidecarindia on October 5, 2026: "There’s a lot of Delhi in a Sunday afternoon spent at Daryaganj.

From academics looking for prized competitive books, to novel-hunting bibliophiles, and the ones on the lookout for the latest copy of Archie’s — this legendary book market brings them all together every week, like clockwork.

The Sunday Book Bazaar transports us to that world and tells the story of Daryaganj’s pavement book market, and the people who read there.

Join author Kanupriya Dhingra in conversation with Chef Sadaf Hussain, a MasterChef India 2016 finalist and author, as they talk about the many stories that come together in the famed Sunday book market.

Join us for conversations on 
25th October, 5–7 PM 
At Sidecar.

₹500 per person, including one non-alcoholic drink.

DM us to book your spot.".

sadaf_hussain on September 23, 2026: "I enjoy cooking karonda and keema together. I love that sudden burst of sourness from the karonda against the richness of the meat. It catches people by surprise.

What surprises me, though, is how many people find the combination unusual, or even a little strange. Perhaps I never thought of it that way because I have been eating it for as long as I can remember. For me, the two simply belong together.

Karonda has a sharp, tart, slightly astringent flavour when it is young, which softens and becomes a little sweeter as the fruit ripens. Native to the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia. 

If you have never tried karonda, I would urge you to. Cook it with meat, turn it into a jam or make a pickle. And if you use karonda in a way I have not tried before, tell me. I would happily try something new.".

148 likes, 18 comments - madameqrie on September 7, 2026: "“The Partition Table”, perhaps a misnomer. 

Sadaf, Urvi, Damini & Team Indicā held the idea of trauma & created a healing afternoon to reckon, retrace, reconnect. We crossed over the lines that divided Punjab, Sindh… Banga… Multan, Delhi… to reach where memory meets imagination. 

Five dishes showcasing how the geography of displacement cannot, and must not, erase the history of community. Nor dampen the fires of culinary ingenuity. When chholey becomes hummus, koki takes a taco turn, and gobindobhog says why khichuri, why not risotto, you know that memory will survive & thrive. 

Thank you for what I will remember as “The Reunion Table”.

@sadaf_hussain @indica.delhi @daminiralleigh @chefurvisharma".

11K likes, 216 comments - pulaowalaa on September 4, 2026: "Bihar ki shaadiyon ka khaana sirf khaana nahi, ek riwayat hai.

Biryani apni jagah hai, lekin Bihar mein Pulao aur Gosht ka apna hi ek andaaz hai — Sonamansoori ka Pulao, halka sa Gosht Kaliya aur saath mein Raita.

Gosht ki tari halki rakhi jaati hai aur Keora ki khushboo ismein apna alag hi taste laati hai.

Aur Bihar ki shaadi mein agar Pulao-Gosht na ho… toh bhai, shaadi mein kuch toh missing hai. 😄

Aap Bihar se hain toh bataiye — aapke yahan bhi shaadi mein Pulao-Gosht zaroor banta hai?

📍 Pulao Wala, Okhla, New Delhi

#PulaoWala #BihariFood #PulaoGosht #BiharCuisine #DelhiFood".

It is not a bed tea but a quick meal to welcome your day, or let's say, silence before the city's noisy streets and busy life embrace you.

Video by @asadonfeeds and special behind the scene appearance by @zaidsyedmohd 😃".

248 likes, 10 comments - indica.delhi on August 29, 2026: "The Partition Table closed last Sunday at indicā — a five-course menu built with chef Sadaf Hussain, tracing how the migrations of 1947 reshaped what was cooked across Punjab, Sindh, Multan, Muslim and Sylheti households, and what was rebuilt in the decades since.

Sunday made one thing clear: seventy-nine years on, 1947 changed not just the lives of those who crossed the border but entirely how a region ate.

#tastingmenu
#historyonourplate #foodcultures #migration #indicadelhi".
